item.title: Women's Only Needle Felting: Sculpting & Painting with Wool — Mon Jul 27, 1:00 PM — The Joel Fund
item.description: When: Mondays, 1:00pm – 4:00pm Dates: Mon: 3/9; 3/16; 3/23 Please Note: All classes and workshops are for Military Connected Individuals who are 18 years or older. This particular class is for military-connected women over 18 years or older. Wool can be used as a medium to paint a landscape or a portrait or be sculpted into a 3-dimensional piece of art! This unique art has been used to illustrate children’s books and in stop-motion animation. Artists have begun to truly appreciate the practicality of using this inexpensive natural resource in ornaments, pin cushions, pillows, hanging art, and much, much more! In this class, students will learn the techniques to make both a flat, 2-dimensional picture and a 3-dimensional sculpture piece. Students will develop self-expression through manipulation of colors and textures of wool. We offer scholarships for those who cannot afford the registration fee. item.title: Aging Gracefully Creative Movement Workshop — Wed Jul 29, 11:00 AM — Arts Together
item.description:
Ages 50+ Aging Gracefully: Meaningful Movement Explorations – As we age it is important to keep the body moving, the brain focused, and the spirit fueled. In this technique/creative dance class, we will do so in a healthy, FUN way. We will warm the body, moving in a way that encourages each dancer to better honor and understand their unique physicality. Next, dancers will explore different ways to generate movement phrases. Inspired by poetry, visual art, and personal experience, we will create dances; accessing the wisdom of the body to express our relationship to the world, each other, and ourselves. No prior dance experience needed, just a willing heart <3

item.title: Lunch & Learn: Intro to Deer Hunting with Artemis Sportswomen — Wed Jul 29, 12:00 PM
item.description: Join North Carolina’s Artemis Sportswomen ambassador Lisa Fierman for an introduction to deer hunting. We invite you to learn more about the relationship between hunting and conservation and the tenets of an ethical hunter. This presentation will include an overview of the skills and knowledge it takes to become a successful deer hunter, and how to find a place to hunt. Artemis Sportswomen is an official program of the National Wildlife Federation and invests in the long-term health and vitality of the sporting world by advancing women’s leadership. By investing in sportswomen’s communities, skills, and leadership, Artemis continues to create an intergenerational cohort of outdoors leaders and champions for hunting and angling. Artemis is dedicated to creating lasting positive impact on sporting and the outdoors, and the land, water, and wildlife upon which we all depend. This Lunch & Learn will be accompanied by a free, in-person deer scouting event on Saturday, August 1 at Bent Cre

Learn about the forest ecology within the various habitats of Brumley that have made this preserve a popular spot for birders, hikers, bikers, and naturalists! item.title: What A Ranger Does - World Ranger Day — Fri Jul 31, 10:00 AM — Near Cliffdwellers
item.description:
Join us as we celebrate World Ranger Day! Our Park Rangers work hard to keep our parks and public lands open, safe, and accessible for all. Did you know that many rangers are also firefighters, EMTs, police officers, and more? Meet a Park Ranger and learn about the many hats a Park Ranger wears.
This touch-a-truck style program will give you a hands-on look at the gear, training, and daily work that goes into protecting the Park.
Around the globe, park rangers are on the front line in the fight to protect our natural heritage. World Ranger Day offers a chance to support their vital work, which ranges from environmental campaigning to education. The day is also an opportunity to pay tribute to rangers who have lost their lives in the line of duty.
***Free with Admission to Chimney Rock Attraction***
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.description:
Experience the history of downtown Durham, strolling between the city’s historic sites. Learn of Durham’s pivotal role in the industrialization of the American South, how a Durham banking magnate transformed the lives of millions of rural farmers, the tobacco factories that powered the city’s future, and much more.
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: Downtown Durham African American Historian-Guided Tour — Sat Aug 1, 4:00 PM — CCB Plaza
item.description:
Durham: the mecca of black capitalism and the center of North Carolina’s African American business community. Join a local historian on this guided walking tour of Durham’s Black Wall Street, hearing the stories of how a humble sharecropper became the owner of the largest black-ned company in American history, and seeing some of the sites related to their stories. Learn how businessmen, labor organizers, educated academics, and craftsmen each contributed to the unique history of Durham’s African American community.
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: Downtown Durham True Crime Walking Tour — Sat Aug 1, 6:00 PM — Lucky Strike Tower
item.description:
From mayoral candidates turned murder suspects, to terrifying cult leaders, to dramatic gangster dramas. Join us on the guided Durham True Crime Tour, hosted by a local historian, and explore the dark side of Durham’s history.
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: Durham Ghost Walk — Sat Aug 1, 8:00 PM — Fate & Folklore
item.description:
Explore the spooky side of Durham’s history on this tour of the city’s most haunted locations. From the disgraced sons of tobacco giants who continue to roam their old factories, to tales of tragic accidents whose victims still haunt the site of their end, and murder victims who stubbornly cling to their possessions, Durham, NC, has a shadowy side to its history. Travel through the city with the assistance of a professional historian guide, while hearing about the city’s creepiest folklore.
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: Schools in Parks — Tue Aug 4, 1:00 PM — Hammocks Beach State Park
item.description:
Schools in Parks: Are you an elementary teacher working with students in grades 3–5 (homeroom, STEM, PE, art, AIG, EC, music, media coordinator, guidance counselor, etc.)? If so, come to the park to learn about the Schools in Parks program. This statewide collaboration between state parks and public schools creates outdoor learning experiences on school campuses and provides tailor-made field trips that are reimbursed. Did we mention that stipends are available for attending workshops and field trips if you are accepted into the program? Plus, you'll earn CEUs and Environmental Education credits! Meet in the Visitor Center auditorium to learn how you may qualify for this partnership.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Scales, Skins and Skeletons — Tue Aug 4, 5:00 PM — Eno River State Park - Fews Ford Access & Visitor Center
item.description:
Have you ever wanted to pet a wild animal? You're in luck! Join us for the Ranger led program and learn about the different animals of the Eno, and get the chance to handle their skins, scales and skeletons!
All children must be accompanied by an adult and bring water!
Spaces are limited, and registration is required. To sign up, call (984) 250-1370 or email eno.river@ncparks.gov. Include the number of guests in your party and a phone number where you can be reached if the event is changed or canceled.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.description:

item.title: NHBA Bird Outing — Wed Aug 5, 7:00 AM
item.description:
For questions, contact Phil Silas at epsdcva@aol.com. The location will be WhippoorwillPark/Warren Creek Trail, 1632 Rowemont Drive, Durham, NC.This outing is sponsored by the New Hope Bird Alliance (formerly New Hope Audubon).Outings usually last 2-3 hours. No reservations or sign-up needed. If there is a large turnout for any particular outing, we may split into two groups. We do recommend carpooling for families or friend pods; while we love pets, there is a ‘no-pet’ policy for bird outings. New birders and birders of all skill levels are welcome. Please wear long pants, socks, and sturdy shoes (ticks and chiggers may be present). Sun and bug protection are also recommended. Bring snacks and water if you like. Heavy rain will result in cancellation.
Source: New Hope Bird Alliance

item.title: Moth Mania — Wed Aug 5, 8:00 PM — Hammocks Beach State Park
item.description:
Moth Mania: Discover the fascinating world of nocturnal insects! Join us as we use special black lights and bright lamps to attract moths and other nighttime insects to a white sheet. Get and up-close look at their incredible colors, patterns, and adaptations while learning about their important role in our local ecosystem. Meet on the back porch of the Visitor’s Center.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Guided Bark Ranger Hike — Thu Aug 6, 10:00 AM — Jones Lake State Park
item.description:
Grab your leash and hit the trail with your four-legged friend! Join us for a fun and informative guided dog hike where you and your pup will explore the park together while learning how to be responsible trail users. Your dog can even become an official NC State Parks Bark Ranger! Treats and special giveaways will be available (while supplies last) for both pups and their humans. All dogs must remain on a leash at all times and should be well-behaved and comfortable around other people and pets.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Pollywogs Storytime — Thu Aug 6, 10:00 AM — Carvers Creek State Park – Long Valley Farm Access
item.description:
Carvers Creek State Park Brings you Carvers Creek Pollywogs. The curriculum for this program is for Preschool and younger, but siblings are always welcome. Please call park office to sign up. We will meet at our secret pond.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Royster Global Keynote Address: “Keeping the Last Page at Bay: A Cat’s Cradle Through Time” — Thu Aug 6, 10:00 AM — FedEx Global Education Center
item.description:
Triple Tar Heel and science communicator Mejs Hasan will deliver the keynote address at the 2026 Royster Global Conference, which is also the celebration of the 30th anniversary of the Royster Society of Fellows.
Today’s challenges, like environmental degradation, migration, and social division, don’t fit neatly within the confines of a single discipline. In order to really address them, we have to cross diverse boundaries, pulling together wisdom from different times, geographies, and subject matters. For 30 years, the Royster Society of Fellows has embodied this spirit of crossing boundaries. It has encouraged and supported collaborations between the science and the humanities, despite their perceived differences.
Being a Royster Fellow gave Mejs Hasan the courage and permission to move between literacy, science, art, and computing; to create science storytelling projects that can bring communities together; to be bold in bringing them to people. It helped Hasan explore how sc

item.title: National Oyster Day "The Day After" — Thu Aug 6, 11:00 AM — Hammocks Beach State Park
item.description:
National Oyster Day "The Day After": Come watch nature’s filtration systems in action as we discuss their role in the estuary and food web, the health benefits to consuming them, and economic value to North Carolina. Joining our Schools in Parks Specialist and the Coastal Education Coordinator from the North Carolina Coastal Federation. No sign up required, meet in the auditorium.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Birding Basics — Fri Aug 7, 8:00 AM — Hammocks Beach State Park
item.description:
Birding Basics: Grab your binoculars and join a park ranger to learn the basics of bird identification. We'll explore how to use binoculars, field guides, and birding apps while practicing observation techniques and discovering the diverse species that call the park home. Meet in the Gazebo outside the Visitor Center.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Dino Dig Live — Fri Aug 7, 12:00 PM — Nature Research Center
item.description:
Every summer the NCMNS paleontology crew goes into the field to search for new fossil specimens and continue digging up previous discoveries. Join us in the SECU Daily Planet Theater in person, or online, for a live video call from a dinosaur quarry! Paleontologists from NCMNS will be live from their fossil quarries across the American West searching for clues to ancient life from millions of years ago from Nebraska to Utah. Join us in-person in the SECU Daily Planet Theater or watch the livestream on YouTube Live. Our live calls (every week this summer!) will give you the chance to join the expedition. You can ask questions and interact with paleontologists in the field. Watch online at the links below.

item.description:
Sensational Snakes: Join us and learn about some of the slithery creatures that call North Carolina home and the important roles they play in our ecosystems. We will discuss key features that can help you determine whether a snake is venomous or nonvenomous, along with other important safety tips. NOTE: program is at Bear Island Concession Stand. item.title: Bird Cruise — Mon Aug 10, 11:00 AM — Hammocks Beach State Park
item.description:
Bird Cruise: Set sail on a guided birding adventure through the waters surrounding Hammocks Beach State Park. This ranger-led excursion will help you identify wading birds, shorebirds, raptors, and seasonal migrants while exploring some of the area's premier birding locations. Bring your binoculars and curiosity as we search for feathered residents and visitors that depend on our estuarine habitats. Limited to 11 participants; sign-up is required. Contact the park to register at 910-326-4881.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Anthony Cole Homestead Hike — Mon Aug 10, 2:30 PM — Eno River State Park - Fews Ford Access & Visitor Center
item.description:
Have you ever hiked on Buckquarter Creek Trail and noticed an old, abandoned cabin? Would you like to know its history? You’re in luck! Hike 2.0 miles with a Ranger to the Anthony Cole Homestead off the Buckquarter Creek Trail to learn about this ruin inside the park.
All children must be accompanied by an adult. Please be sure to dress appropriately for the weather, wear hiking shoes, and bring water!
Spaces are limited, and registration is required. To sign up, call (984) 250-1370 or email eno.river@ncparks.gov. Include the number of guests in your party and a phone number where you can be reached if the event is changed or canceled.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Make Your Own Nature Journal — Tue Aug 11, 10:00 AM — Jones Lake State Park
item.description:
Join park staff for a fun, hands-on craft where you'll create a personalized nature journal from start to finish! Participants will make their own recycled paper, decorate a journal cover, and learn how keeping a nature journal can help you notice the amazing plants and animals all around you! Supplies are limited, and registration is required. Call park office at (910)- 588-4550 to register. All ages welcome!
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Summer Meteor Shower: Perseids — Wed Aug 12, 5:00 AM — Eno River State Park - Fews Ford Access & Visitor Center
item.description:
Every year, Earth travels through a debris field left behind by a Sun-orbiting comet resulting in amazing meteor showers that light up the pre-dawn July and August skies. Join a Ranger to learn about these and other fiery space objects and then enjoy the show!
Leave when you need to!
Bring a chair or blanket as the best viewing will be lying down! All children must be accompanied by an adult. Please be sure to dress appropriately for the weather, wear bug spray, bring water and snacks!
Spaces are limited, and registration is required. To sign up, call (984) 250-1370 or email eno.river@ncparks.gov. Include the number of guests in your party and a phone number where you can be reached if the event is changed or canceled.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Kayak with a Ranger — Wed Aug 12, 8:30 AM — Hammocks Beach State Park
item.description:
Kayak with a Ranger: Join a ranger-led kayaking tour through the estuary, beginning promptly at 8:30 a.m. and ending at 11:30 a.m. This program is limited to 10 participants, with a minimum age requirement of 13. Sign-up is required. Attendees will meet at the picnic table near the kayak launch. To register, contact the park at 910-326-4881.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Eco Cruise — Wed Aug 12, 11:00 AM — Hammocks Beach State Park
item.description:
Eco Cruise: Climb aboard for a guided cruise through the rich estuarine habitats surrounding Hammocks Beach State Park. This ranger-led adventure will explore the plants, animals, and natural processes that make our coastal ecosystems so unique. Keep an eye out for birds, dolphins, crabs, and other wildlife as we discuss the importance of estuaries and their role in supporting life along the North Carolina coast. Limited to 11 participants; sign-up is required. Contact the park to register at 910-326-4881.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Thursday Community Board Game night at Moondog Meadery — Thu Aug 13, 7:00 PM

It's a bit smaller group than the large Monday night extravaganza, and there are a lot of drop in and independent groups here as well. Moondog has an extensive and ever-changing collection of games that are usually loaned out for a fee, but on Thursdays (just like on Mondays), they are all free to play. item.title: Moth Night at Carolina Beach State Park — Thu Aug 13, 8:30 PM — Carolina Beach State Park
item.description:
Join the North Carolina Wildlife Federation at Carolina Beach State Park for National Moth Week! Meet some moths you may have never seen before and listen for nocturnal birds in the coastal fringe forest of southeastern NC. Learn to use Seek and iNaturalist to identify and record species sightings. Upload 10 species observations to get your NC Moth Week badge!
**Event rescheduled to Thursday, August 13th**
This event is FREE and open to the public. Registration is required: https://wl.donorperfect.net/weblink/weblink.aspx?name=E12185&id=1206
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Backyard Birds — Fri Aug 14, 9:00 AM — Carvers Creek State Park – Long Valley Farm Access
item.description:
Join us to learn how to make your home a safe and healthy place for birds! We'll review educational materials and discuss ways to create bird-friendly habitats in your own backyard. While adults participate, kids can make homemade bird feeders to take home and enjoy.
Important: We will be using peanut butter for the bird feeders. If anyone in your party has a nut allergy, please let us know in advance so we can provide a suitable alternative. Where: Meet at the Visitor Center parking lot. From there, we will make our way to the Secret Pond location. We hope you'll join us for this fun and educational program! 🐦🌿
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Lizards on the Loose! — Fri Aug 14, 2:00 PM — Hammocks Beach State Park
item.description:
Lizards on the Loose: From speedy skinks to color changing anoles, North Carolina's lizards are full of surprises! Celebrate World Lizard Day with a park ranger as we explore the local species, discover their unique adaptations, and learn about their role in coastal ecosystems. Meet on the back patio of the Visitor Center.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Bark - Tree Identification — Fri Aug 14, 2:30 PM — Occoneechee Mountain State Natural Area
item.description:
Have you ever been curious about Tree Identification but didn’t exactly know where to start? You’re not alone! Hike 1.5 miles with a Ranger along the Occoneechee Mountain Loop, Brown Elfin Knob, and Chestnut Oak trails to learn how to identify trees.
All children must be accompanied by an adult. Please be sure to dress appropriately for the weather, wear hiking shoes, and bring water!
Spaces are limited, and registration is required. To sign up, call (984) 250-1370 or email eno.river@ncparks.gov. Include the number of guests in your party and a phone number where you can be reached if the event is changed or canceled.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Canoe Hike — Sat Aug 15, 9:00 AM — Carvers Creek State Park – Long Valley Farm Access
item.description:
We will be learning the basics of canoeing and then trying out our new skills by maneuvering through the Cypress swamp. This is a slow and calm canoeing experience and great for beginners or if you want to get a closer look at the Cypress trees. YOU MUST SIGN-UP. You can call the park office to sign-up. Limit is 10 visitors. Please allow approximately 15 minutes to walk from the parking lot to the Rain Shelter. Age requirement- 8 years old and older.

item.description:

The location is 316 Gee Building, 1247 Jimmie Kerr Road, Graham, NC 27253. The exhibit profiles 6 ancestors of the Scott family of the Hawfields, describing their experiences/contributions to the American Revolution.
